problems.title: Distance between graph intersections
problems.question: Find the distance between intersections of y=x² and y=5x−6.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: The intersection points are(2,4) and(3,9). Their distance is √[(3−2)²+(9−4)²].

problems.title: Substitute a known root
problems.question: One root of x²−ax+6=0 is 1. Find a.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Thus a=7.

problems.title: Symmetric biquadratic roots
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of y⁴−5y²+1=0.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: With $t=y^2$, the equation is $t^2-5t+1=0$, whose roots $(5\pm\sqrt{21})/2$ are both positive.
steps: Each positive t gives a pair of opposite y values. Each pair sums to 0.

problems.title: Complementary sine squares
problems.question: Evaluate $\sin^225°+\sin^265°$.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Substitute the complementary cosine and apply the identity.

problems.title: Divide by a cosine
problems.question: Find $(3\sin\alpha+2\cos\alpha)/(5\sin\alpha-4\cos\alpha)$ if tanα=3.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: Tangent being defined gives $\cos\alpha\ne0$. Divide numerator and denominator by it.
steps: The quotient is(3tanα+2)/(5tanα−4)=(9+2)/(15−4).

problems.title: Cosine of the smallest triangle angle
problems.question: Triangle sides are 7,9,10. Find the cosine of its smallest angle.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: The smallest angle is opposite 7. The cosine rule gives $\cos A=(9^2+10^2-7^2)/(2\cdot9\cdot10)$.
steps: The numerator is 132 and denominator 180. Reduce.

problems.title: Count solution pairs
problems.question: How many real pairs satisfy $3x^2-7xy+4y^2=0$, xy=5?
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: If x=y, xy=5 gives(√5,√5) and(−√5,−√5). If x=4y/3, then y²=15/4, giving two more pairs with x/y=4/3. The two branches cannot overlap when xy=5.

problems.title: Speeds from post-meeting travel times
problems.question: A motorcyclist and cyclist start toward each other 60 km apart. After meeting, the motorcyclist takes 1 hour to finish and the cyclist 4 hours. Find their speed sum.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: Let speeds be u, v and meeting time t. The remaining distances give $u=vt$ and $4v=ut$.
steps: Thus t²=4 and t=2 hours. Since they jointly cover 60 km before meeting, u+v=60/2.

problems.title: Two trigonometric roots
problems.question: The roots x₁, x₂ satisfy $x^2-x\cos\alpha=x\sin\alpha-\sin\alpha\cos\alpha$. Find x₁/x₂.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: The roots are sinα and cosα. If x₁=sinα, x₂=cosα, the quotient is tanα when cosα≠0. Reversing their labels gives cotα when sinα≠0.
problems.answer: Intended ordered ratio: tanα; the unordered-root data do not fix it.
problems.note: No ordering of x₁, x₂ is specified, and zero denominator cases are not excluded. A unique tanα answer needs x₁=sinα, x₂=cosα and cosα≠0.

problems.title: Possible cosine sum in a right triangle
problems.question: Which listed value can be the sum of cosines of the acute angles of a right triangle?
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: The acute angles are θ,90°−θ, so the sum is $\sin\theta+\cos\theta\le\sqrt2$.
steps: Its possible range is(1,√2]. Among the printed choices only √2 lies in this range; it occurs at θ=45°.

problems.title: Recognise a square of a quadratic
problems.question: Find the product of distinct roots of $(x^2+3x+1)(x^2+3x+3)+1=0$.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Thus x²+3x+2=0, with distinct roots −1 and −2. Their product is 2.
problems.note: The reduced roots each have multiplicity 2 in the original quartic. Counting multiplicity would give product 4; the listed answer 2 counts distinct solutions.

problems.title: Cancel but retain a forbidden point
problems.question: Find the product of roots of $|(x^2-x-2)/(x-2)|=|2x+5|$.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: For x≠2, the left side is $|x+1|$. Equal absolute values give $x+1=\pm(2x+5)$.
steps: The roots are −4 and −2, both permitted. Multiply them.

problems.title: A quadratic in the absolute value
problems.question: Find the product of roots of $4x^2+\sqrt{x^2}+2|x|-7=0$.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Only t=1 is nonnegative, so x=±1.

problems.title: A side from the sine rule
problems.question: In ABC, AC=6, C=30°, A=15°. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.

problems.title: A parallelogram’s two sides
problems.question: Parallelogram diagonals are √21,√61; one side is 1 longer than the other. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: The parallelogram law gives $2(a^2+b^2)=21+61=82$. Put b=a+1.
steps: a²+(a+1)²=41 gives a²+a−20=0. The positive root is 4, so b=5. Perimeter=2(4+5).

problems.title: Root separation parameter
problems.question: Find the product of all a for which x²−ax+10=0 has real roots differing in absolute value by 3.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Set a²−40=9, obtaining a=±7. Both give discriminant 9 and meet the condition. Their product is −49.

problems.title: Remainder at a linear factor
problems.question: Find the remainder of x⁵+x⁴−3x³+2x²+x+1 divided by x−1.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Evaluate 1+1−3+2+1+1.

problems.title: Product of cubic roots
problems.question: Find the product of roots of 2x³−9x²+7x+6=0.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: For a cubic $ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$, the root product is $-d/a$.
steps: Here−d/a=−6/2=−3. Indeed the polynomial factors as(x−2)(2x+1)(x−3), so all three roots are real.

problems.title: A root condition incompatible over the reals
problems.question: For which a do the real roots of x²−2x+a=0 have cube sum −4?
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: The formal equation 8−6a=−4 gives a=2. But the quadratic discriminant then is 4−8=−4, so its roots are not real. In fact real roots require a≤1 and then the cube sum is at least 2.
problems.answer: No such a for real roots.
problems.note: If complex roots were allowed, a=2 would work, with roots 1±i. The standard real-root interpretation gives the printed “no such a” choice.

problems.title: Perpendicular crossing chords
problems.question: Circle chords AB, CD are perpendicular. AC=6, BC=5, BD=3. Find AD.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: At their crossing K, Pythagoras gives $AC^2+BD^2=AD^2+BC^2$.
steps: Both sides of this identity contain the same four squared distances AK², BK², CK², DK². Thus AD²=36+9−25=20.

problems.title: Polynomial remainder modulo a quadratic
problems.question: Find the remainder of x⁵−x⁴−x³+5x²−4x+5 divided by x²−x+1.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Substitute these remainders:(1−x)−(−x)−(−1)+5(x−1)−4x+5=x+2. Its degree is less than 2.

problems.title: Use a cubic relation to reduce powers
problems.question: Evaluate $x^{10}+2x^9+2x^8+x^7+x^6+x^5$ if $x^3+x^2=1$.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
steps: Using x³+x²=1, also x⁵+x⁴=x² and x⁷+x⁶=x⁴. Thus the second factor is x⁴+x⁵+x³=x²+x³=1. Both factors are 1.

problems.title: A subset condition and an empty solution set
problems.question: Find the product of all integer a for which the solution set of $|x-3|=a-4$ is a subset of the roots of $(x^2-6x+5)(x-3)=0$.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: The target root set is $\{1,3,5\}$. For a<4 the absolute equation has the empty solution set, which is a subset of every set.
steps: Thus every integer a<4 qualifies. At a=4 the root is 3; at a=6 the roots are 1,5; no other a≥4 works. The full parameter set is therefore all integers a≤4 together with 6, an infinite set.
problems.answer: As written, no finite product is defined. With a nonempty-solution requirement, the intended product is 4·6=24.
problems.note: The source does not exclude the empty solution set. That missing condition is needed for the listed finite answer 24.

problems.title: Three cevians divide one angle into quarters
problems.question: An altitude, internal bisector and median from vertex B divide angle B into four equal parts. Find |A−C|.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: Write $B=4t$. Interchanging A, C if needed, the altitude, bisector and median occur at angles t,2t,3t from BA. Place the altitude vertically and AC horizontally at height 1.
steps: Then A=(−tan t,1), C=(tan 3t,1), and the median has horizontal-to-vertical ratio tan 2t. Because its foot is the base midpoint, tan 3t−tan t=2tan2t.
Use tan 3t−tan t=sin 2t/(cos 3t cos t). Cancelling positive sin 2t yields cos 2t=2cos3t cos t=cos 4t+cos 2t. Hence cos 4t=0. Since 0<B=4t<180°, B=90° and t=22.5°.
The base angles are 90°−t=67.5° and 90°−3t=22.5°. Their difference is 45°.

problems.title: Two triangles on opposite sides of a common base
problems.question: AB=BC, triangles ABC and DBC are on opposite sides of BC, DBC=DCB=20°, and ADC=100°. Find BCA.
problems.idea: Use identities, root relations, or a direct geometric calculation.
formulas: Let γ=BCA=BAC and β=ABC=180°−2γ. Triangle DBC has angle D=140°. The given 100° at D leaves $ADB=40°$.
steps: The sine rule in ABD and DBC gives AB/BD=sin 40°/sin BAD and BD/BC=sin 20°/sin 140°. Since AB=BC and sin 140°=sin 40°, multiplication gives sin BAD=sin 20°.
Because BAD is part of the acute isosceles base angle γ<90°, BAD=20°. Hence ABD=180−40−20=120°. Since ABD=ABC+CBD=β+20°, β=100° and γ=(180−100)/2.
